title: OTF-1 (Overby Telemetry Format v1)
description: Canonical schema for real-time reporting of Overby Industries mining, reclamation, and certification telemetry, and for the fleet-coordination packets exchanged between vehicle/pod nodes and a fleet coordinator. See README.md for the full field-by-field rationale.

kind.description: Which packet this is. Omitted means "event", so every packet written before the fleet kinds existed is still valid unchanged.

timestamp.description: UTC ISO-8601 timestamp. For an event, when it happened; for every other kind, when the sender transmitted the packet.

taskAction.description: What a node is asked to do. Each value is the imperative of an event action: a completed "capture" task is reported as a "captured" event, "process" as "processed", and so on.

seq.description: Per-source counter, increasing across every fleet packet that source sends. A receiver orders a source's packets by timestamp first and seq second, and discards any that are not newer than what it has already applied -- duplicates and out-of-order arrivals are routine over light-delayed, store-and-forward links. Timestamp comes first so that a source which restarts and counts from 0 again is still understood.

event.description: Something that happened to material: a capture, a processing run, a deployment. This is the original OTF-1 packet and the one the public record is built from.

target.description: Present for debris-capture events (mission.type = reclaimer). Omitted for mining/refinery processing events that have no single tracked object.

SMESSC.description: Space Mining Environmental, Safety & Sustainability Certification compliance flag for this event.

ODCI_contribution.description: Incremental contribution (kg) to the Orbital Debris Cleanup Index, if applicable.

ProofOfCleanupToken.description: Blockchain token id proving this event's outcome, if issued.

taskId.description: The assignment this event completes, when the work was assigned by a fleet coordinator. Omitted for work a node did on its own initiative.

status.description: A node's periodic report of its own state. It is a complete snapshot rather than a delta, so a coordinator that missed any number of earlier packets is fully caught up by the next one it receives.

mode.description: Health as the node itself judges it. nominal: available for work. degraded: finishing what it holds, taking nothing new. safe: local fault response has taken over and any held task is abandoned.

phase.description: Name of the node's local control state, reported verbatim (for a shuttle, a ShuttleFSM state such as "OrbitalCruise"). Informative only: a coordinator must never branch on it.

link.description: The node's own view of coordinator contact. autonomous: it has stopped hearing the coordinator and is running on local defaults, even though this packet may still get through.

capabilities.description: Task actions this node can perform. Advertised by the node so a coordinator needs no built-in table of node types.

task.description: The task the node is working on, or the last one it finished. Kept in every status until a newer task replaces it, so an outcome is never lost with a single dropped packet. Omitted only by a node that has never held a task.

heartbeat.description: Minimal liveness signal from either side. A node that stops hearing coordinator heartbeats falls back to its local defaults; it never waits for one before acting on a fault.

assignment.description: A coordinator offering one task to one node. It is an offer, not a command: the node's local control has the final say and answers with an ack.

destination.description: Id of the node this offer is for.

acceptBy.description: The node must refuse the offer if it arrives after this instant. This bounds how stale an offer can be when it finally lands, and it is what lets a coordinator conclude from a later status that the offer was not taken.

ack.description: A node's answer to an assignment.

destination.description: Id of the coordinator that made the offer.

reason.description: Why the offer was rejected. busy and expired are transient; unsupported and refused mean this node should not be offered this task again.
